references.text: Jesus says in the Sermon on the Mount that if the light within you is darkness, how deep will that darkness be. [ref:Matt 6:23|Matthew 6:23] is a direct parallel where Jesus warns that the inner light can become darkness, which corresponds to the warning in Luke 11:35.

Isaiah warns against those who call darkness light and light darkness ([ref:Isa 5:20|Isaiah 5:20]). This is a prophetic warning about confusing light and darkness, reflecting Jesus' exhortation to ensure that the light within one is not darkness.

Paul describes how people who knew God became darkened in their foolish hearts and became fools while claiming to be wise ([ref:Rom 1:21-22|Romans 1:21-22]). This illustrates the danger of what should have been light and insight turning into darkness.

John writes that the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it ([ref:John 1:5|John 1:5]). The contrast between light and darkness is central also in Luke 11:35, where the warning concerns ensuring that the inner light is not extinguished.

Jesus says that the light has come into the world, but people loved darkness more than light ([ref:John 3:19-20|John 3:19-20]). This shows how people can actively choose darkness over light, which is at the heart of the warning in Luke 11:35.

Paul reminds the Ephesians that they once were darkness, but now are light in the Lord ([ref:Eph 5:8|Ephesians 5:8]). The contrast between darkness and light in the believer underscores the same warning Jesus gives in Luke 11:35 about guarding one's inner light.

John writes that God is light and there is no darkness in him, and warns against walking in darkness while claiming to have fellowship with him ([ref:1 John 1:5-6|1 John 1:5-6]). This is a parallel warning against self-deception regarding light and darkness, as Jesus exhorts in Luke 11:35.
